title: Testing evidence and user guide
one: The two short chapters of the write-up this guide covers.
marks: This chapter is where the examiner looks for tests that try the edges of each rule, for a picture that proves what happened in each test, for a mistake that was found, fixed and tested again, and for a guide that a member of staff could follow without help.

screens.title: See what you will make in this chapter.

blocks.p: Your program works. This chapter turns that into two of the things you hand in. The first piece is your testing evidence: a table of tests in Word, with a picture under it for each test. The second piece is a user guide: a short document that shows a member of staff how to use each window of your program.

There is no code in this chapter. You use your running program, the Snipping Tool and Word. Most of the tests are ones you have already ticked at the end of chapters 7, 8 and 9, so the work here is writing them down and taking the pictures.

need: Chapters 7, 8 and 9 are finished, and every row of their test tables is ticked.
Your BikeShop solution is open in Visual Studio 2019, and it builds.
Word is open with a new, empty document.
This guide is open in the Edge browser beside you. Tick each step as you do it, and the chapter remembers where you are.

words: Test
One thing you do to your program, written down with what should happen and what did happen.
Test table
A table in Word with one row for each test.
Valid data
Data the program should accept, such as a booking in a free slot.
Invalid data
Data the program should refuse, such as a booking on a Sunday.
Extreme data
Data right on the edge of what is allowed, such as selling exactly the number in stock. It should be accepted.
Boundary
The edge between allowed and refused, such as the moment one booking ends and the next one starts.
Expected result
What should happen, written before you run the test.
Actual result
What did happen when you ran the test.
Evidence
A picture of the screen that proves the actual result.
Corrective action
What you changed when a test did not give the expected result, and the test run again afterwards.
User guide
A short document that shows a member of staff how to use each window of your program.
Snipping Tool
The program on the Start menu that takes a picture of part of the screen.

screens.title: Read the eight columns of the test table, and six real rows.

blocks.p: A test table has eight columns. Test is the number of the test. What is tested says what the test is about, in a few words. Type says whether the data is valid, invalid or extreme. What you do says exactly what you type or press. Expected result is what should happen. Actual result is what did happen. Evidence names the picture that proves it. Fixed? says what you changed, if anything was wrong.

Here are six rows, taken from the test tables at the end of chapters 7 and 8. The words are the same words you ticked there. Rows 1 to 3 are about bookings, and rows 4 to 6 are about stock and the workshop days. Row 5 is the one that went wrong the first time, and stage 2 shows how it was put right.

box.title: Test 1: A booking in a free slot
box.text: Type: valid. What you do: New booking, a free mechanic, a free time. Expected result: It appears in the grid. Actual result: As expected. Evidence: Figure 1, the diary with the new booking in it. Fixed?: Nothing to fix.

box.title: Test 2: The same mechanic, the same start time
box.text: Type: invalid. What you do: Book it again for the same mechanic. Expected result: Message: That mechanic already has a booking in that time. Actual result: As expected. Evidence: Figure 2, the message box. Fixed?: Nothing to fix.

box.title: Test 3: A booking that starts exactly when another ends
box.text: Type: extreme. What you do: Start at the first booking's end time. Expected result: Allowed: touching is not overlapping. Actual result: As expected. Evidence: Figure 3, the diary with both bookings in it. Fixed?: Nothing to fix.

box.title: Test 4: Sell more than is in stock
box.text: Type: invalid. What you do: Pick PADS-DISC with 2 in stock, Sell, quantity 3. Expected result: Message: Only 2 in stock. Actual result: As expected. Evidence: Figure 4, the message box. Fixed?: Nothing to fix.

box.title: Test 5: Sell exactly what is in stock
box.text: Type: extreme. What you do: PADS-DISC, Sell, quantity 2. Expected result: The row shows 0, and it is pink. Actual result: The first time, the sale was refused with the message Only 2 in stock. After the fix, as expected. Evidence: Figure 5, the wrong refusal, and Figure 6, the row showing 0 after the fix. Fixed?: Yes. The check in usp_PartSale_Add said <= where it should say <. It was changed to <, and the test was run again.

box.title: Test 6: A Sunday
box.text: Type: invalid. What you do: Pick a Sunday. Expected result: Message: The workshop is closed on Sundays. Actual result: As expected. Evidence: Figure 7, the message box. Fixed?: Nothing to fix.

stages.title: Which tests to show, and how to show a fix

screens.title: Choose the tests that try the edges of each rule.

blocks.p: You cannot show every test you ran, and you do not need to. The examiner is looking for the tests that try the edges. A test in the middle, such as one booking on an empty day, shows very little. A test right on the edge shows that you thought about where the rule stops.

box.title: The tests to show first
box.text: Two bookings that touch: one starts at the exact minute the other ends. It must be allowed. Selling exactly the number in stock: the count goes down to 0. It must be allowed. The refusals: the same mechanic at the same time, selling more than is in stock, a Sunday, a time that has passed, refunding the same sale twice. Each one must be refused with its own sentence. The reports: the From date after the To date, and two days with nothing in them.

rule.text: Show the test where two bookings touch and the test where they overlap by 15 minutes. Together they prove that the line between allowed and refused is in the right place.
Show the test that sells exactly what is in stock and the test that sells one more. Together they prove that the count can reach 0 and can never go below it.

blocks.p: For each rule, aim for at least one valid row, one invalid row and one extreme row. The six rows in stage 1 do that for bookings. For stock they give an invalid row and an extreme row, so use the chapter 8 test that sells 1 of CHAIN-9 as the valid row.

screens.title: Show a fix in three pictures: the test, the fix, the retest.

blocks.p: A test that fails is not a problem in your write-up. A failed test that you found, fixed and tested again is some of the best evidence you can show, because it proves that the testing was real. The examiner calls this corrective action.

Test 5 is a real example. The check in usp_PartSale_Add was typed as IF @InStock <= @Quantity. With 2 pairs of disc brake pads in stock, a sale of 2 was refused, and the message said Only 2 in stock. That message makes no sense: 2 in stock is enough for a sale of 2. That is the clue that the edge is in the wrong place.

screens.title: Read what goes on each page of the user guide.

blocks.p: The user guide is for the people in the scenario, not for the examiner and not for a programmer. Write it for a member of staff on their first day at Towpath Cycles. There is no code in it, and no table names.

Give each window of your program one page. The sign-in window comes first, because it is the first thing anyone sees, then the main menu, then each window in the order a member of staff would meet it. Every page has the same three parts.

box.title: The three parts of every page
box.text: What it is for: one or two sentences that say what the window does for the shop. The steps: numbered steps, each one starting with a doing word, such as Type, Pick or Press, with a picture of the window. What can go wrong: each message the window can show, word for word, and what to do about it.

blocks.p: The pictures come from your own running program, taken with the Snipping Tool, the same way as your test pictures. A picture of the window with real names and numbers in it is worth more than a paragraph of description.

screens.title: Read the sign-in page, the first page of the guide.

blocks.p: Here is the first page of the Towpath Cycles user guide. Yours follows the same pattern with your own names and messages.

box.title: Page 1: Signing in
box.text: What it is for: The sign-in window lets a member of staff into the program. Each person has their own username, so the program can record who made each booking, hire and sale. The steps: 1. Type your username in the Username box. 2. Type your password in the Password box. It shows as dots. 3. Press Sign in, or press Enter. The main menu opens with your name at the top. What can go wrong: If you press Sign in with a box empty, the message Type your username and your password. appears, and you fill in both boxes. If the username or the password is wrong, the message Those details are not recognised. Check them and try again. appears, and the password box is emptied. If the program cannot reach the database, the message Could not reach the database. Is SQL Server running? appears, and you ask the manager.

blocks.p: Every row below checks one thing the examiner will look for. Three rows are marked Must be refused. check.what: The test table has its eight headings

Read down the Type column. Every row says valid, invalid or extreme, and each rule has at least one of each.

check.what: The touching-booking test catches the mistake
check.how: 1. In usp_Appointment_Add in SSMS, change the check to @StartTime <= EndTime. 2. Select the stored procedure and press F5. 3. Book the same mechanic at the end time of one of their bookings. The message reads: That mechanic already has a booking in that time. 4. Change the check back to @StartTime < EndTime, select the stored procedure and press F5 again.

check.what: The exact-stock test catches the mistake

blocks.p: Nine ticks are your evidence that the test table and the user guide are complete. When you want the sample data back, click in BikeShop.sql and press F5 with nothing selected.

box.title: Make it yours
box.text: Your scenario has its own two rules. First, write down the edge of each one: the exact moment two of your bookings touch, and the exact count that empties your stock. Next, write one valid row, one invalid row and one extreme row for each rule in your test table, before you run them, with the expected result filled in. Last, list every window of your program in the order a member of staff would meet them. That list is the contents page of your user guide.
